comparison: Both evaluate background and contextual claims (C1-C3, C8-C28, C83-C86, C96-C97, C110-C111). OpenEval and peer reviewers agree these are SUPPORTED as accurate representations of established knowledge with appropriate citations. High concordance with 91.2% claim overlap.

Both address bulk vs. individual screening comparison (C56-C64, C90). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED with reasonable trade-offs noted. Peer reviewers express UNCERTAINTY, questioning efficiency (only 13 cross-reactive clones from 77 sorted cells) and whether the approach is as efficient as claimed. Significant disagreement on interpretation.

Both evaluate the dual-expression vector system development (C4-C5, C30-C32, C45-C49). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED based on experimental data. Peer reviewers also find SUPPORTED, explicitly affirming it as 'highly efficient' and 'elegantly merging newer technologies.' Peer result also includes C98-C103 (system innovation and technical advantages) which OpenEval addresses separately. Strong agreement.

Both evaluate antibody characterization (C66-C74 in OpenEval; C66-C74, C79-C80, C93-C95 in peer review). Both find SUPPORTED. OpenEval focuses on SPR affinity data and broad reactivity. Peer reviewers accept SPR validation and differential binding patterns as evidence against His-tag specificity. Strong agreement with peer review covering additional related claims.

Both address experimental efficiency metrics. OpenEval evaluates C6, C35, C38-C40, C51-C53, C87-C89 as SUPPORTED, emphasizing 7-day timeline and 75.9% cloning efficiency. Peer reviewers evaluate C51-C55, C87-C89 as SUPPORTED without challenge, though concerns about overall conversion efficiency appear in peer R4. Moderate agreement with some claim overlap.

Partial overlap on antibody isolation demonstration. OpenEval R3 covers C6, C35, C38-C40 (among others) as SUPPORTED. Peer R2 covers C6, C33-C35, C38-C40, C82 as SUPPORTED, affirming rapid isolation feasibility and suitability for cross-reactive antibodies. Both agree on successful demonstration with 35.7% claim overlap.

Both address core screening system innovation. OpenEval R2 evaluates C29, C33-C34, C43-C44, C98-C100 as SUPPORTED. Peer R6 evaluates C29, C43-C44, C104, C107-C109 as SUPPORTED, affirming overall utility but noting limited novelty compared to published methods. Agreement on technical feasibility with peer reviewers adding context about incremental advancement.

Both address future applications and speculative claims. OpenEval evaluates C7, C41-C42, C107-C109 as UNCERTAIN, noting lack of direct experimental validation for human applications and pandemic response. Peer reviewers evaluate C7, C41-C42, C112-C114 as SUPPORTED, accepting potential applications without critical evaluation of speculative nature. Disagreement on how to treat forward-looking claims.

Both address speculative future developments. OpenEval evaluates C112-C114 (automation predictions) as UNCERTAIN with no experimental support. Peer R7 includes these claims in SUPPORTED evaluation of potential applications. Disagreement: OpenEval distinguishes speculation from demonstrated results, while peer reviewers accept forward-looking statements.

Partial overlap on antibody characterization. OpenEval R6 evaluates C76-C80, C82 as SUPPORTED regarding A6p4 similarity to C179. Peer R5 includes C79-C80 in broader characterization evaluation as SUPPORTED. Both agree on competition assay data and phylogenetic findings.

Both address genetic feature analysis. OpenEval evaluates C54-C55 as SUPPORTED but notes limited generalizability of the inference about broad reactivity not requiring unique genetic features. Peer R3 includes C54-C55 in SUPPORTED evaluation without challenging the generalization. Mild disagreement on scope of conclusions.

Both address His-tag binding artifact concerns. OpenEval evaluates C92-C95 as SUPPORTED, finding evidence against His-tag binding through differential binding patterns. Peer R5 includes C93-C95 in SUPPORTED characterization, implicitly accepting differential binding as evidence against His-tag specificity. Agreement on this control.

Partial overlap on technical advantages. OpenEval R9 evaluates C101-C104 as SUPPORTED regarding dual vector efficiency and Golden Gate reliability. Peer R1 includes C101-C103 in broader SUPPORTED evaluation of methodological development. Agreement on technical merits.

Minimal overlap on system innovation. OpenEval R2 evaluates C98-C100 (linking membrane antibody to genetic information) as SUPPORTED. Peer R1 includes these claims in broader SUPPORTED evaluation of the dual-expression system. Agreement on core innovation.

Minimal overlap on speed advantage. OpenEval R2 evaluates C33-C34 (7-day timeline) as SUPPORTED. Peer R2 includes C33-C34 in SUPPORTED evaluation of rapid antibody isolation. Agreement on demonstrated timeline.

Minimal overlap on quantitative outcomes. OpenEval R10 evaluates C90-C91 as SUPPORTED (enrichment from 284 to 13 clones). Peer R4 includes C90 in UNCERTAIN evaluation, questioning whether the conversion rate demonstrates efficiency as claimed. Disagreement on interpretation of the same enrichment data.

Minimal overlap. OpenEval R6 evaluates C82 (A6p4 functional similarity to C179) as SUPPORTED. Peer R2 includes C82 in broader SUPPORTED evaluation of antibody isolation demonstration. Agreement on this specific finding.

Both address citation of prior work. OpenEval R11 evaluates C105-C106 (Lima et al., 2022 citation) as SUPPORTED as appropriate acknowledgment. Peer R9 includes these claims in background statements accepted as SUPPORTED. Agreement on appropriate citation.

Minimal overlap. OpenEval R9 evaluates C104 (fluorescence-affinity correlation) as SUPPORTED though noting need for stronger quantitative validation. Peer R6 includes C104 in SUPPORTED evaluation of overall system utility. Agreement on general correlation.

Partial overlap on application claims. OpenEval R12 evaluates C107-C109 (acceleration and utility claims) as UNCERTAIN without broader validation. Peer R6 evaluates these as SUPPORTED, affirming utility for pandemic preparedness. Disagreement on whether demonstrated proof-of-concept sufficiently supports broad application claims.

Minimal overlap. OpenEval R15 includes C110 (throughput limitation) in background claims as SUPPORTED. Peer R8 evaluates C110 as SUPPORTED limitation explicitly acknowledged by reviewers. Agreement that this limitation is recognized.

OpenEval evaluates C75 (speculation about stem-negative antibody binding sites) as UNCERTAIN without epitope mapping data. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific speculative claim.

OpenEval evaluates C36-C37 (established knowledge about broadly reactive antibodies and need for large-scale screening) as SUPPORTED background context. No corresponding specific peer review evaluation found, though these claims may be implicitly accepted in peer background evaluations.
OpenEval evaluates C50 (experimental materials description) as SUPPORTED methodological detail. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this routine methodological claim.

Peer reviewers explicitly acknowledge C110 as a SUPPORTED limitation regarding well-based system throughput constraints, noting 'significant loss of cells during FACs, transfection and cloning efficiency are critical to success.' OpenEval addresses C110 in R15 as background context rather than as a distinct limitation evaluation.
